```{r}
library(tidyverse)

nhanes <- read_csv("examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv")

r_summary <- nhanes |>
  filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup), !is.na(Gender)) |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup, Gender) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = round(mean(BMI), 2),
    sd_bmi = round(sd(BMI), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(IncomeGroup, Gender)

r_summary
```

```{r}
summarise_mean_sd <- function(data, value, group1, group2) {
  data |>
    filter(!is.na({{ value }}), !is.na({{ group1 }}), !is.na({{ group2 }})) |>
    group_by({{ group1 }}, {{ group2 }}) |>
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      mean_value = round(mean({{ value }}), 2),
      sd_value = round(sd({{ value }}), 2),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange({{ group1 }}, {{ group2 }})
}

r_function_summary <- summarise_mean_sd(nhanes, BMI, IncomeGroup, Gender)
as.data.frame(r_function_summary)
```


```{r}
# Exercise: swap the value column (BMI -> Weight)
as.data.frame(summarise_mean_sd(nhanes, Weight, IncomeGroup, Gender))

# Exercise: swap a grouping column (IncomeGroup -> EducationClean)
as.data.frame(summarise_mean_sd(nhanes, BMI, EducationClean, Gender))
```


```{r}
# Parity checks (textbook Part D)
nrow(nhanes)
ncol(nhanes)
nrow(filter(nhanes, !is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup), !is.na(Gender)))
nrow(r_summary)
```


## Parity Discussion

The Python/pandas translation in `translation.ipynb` matches this R summary on every check: raw row count (105,626), raw column count (18), filtered row count (87,647), number of groups (6), group labels, and `n`, `mean_bmi`, and `sd_bmi` after rounding to 2 decimals. The full comparison is in `parity-table.csv`.
